## Historical audit: S0032, visible chunk 1 of 2

**Source:** `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_v2/results/r1/fixed_h0/H0/selection/commons_186238614/trajectory.jsonl`. Citations below refer to its JSONL lines. The reference and render images themselves are not visible in this audit.

| Evidence | Observed operations and results |
|---|---|
| Goal | The student was instructed to reconstruct a single 512 × 342 indoor photograph with separate meshes and a matched camera, without using the image as a texture or background (line 1, `model_request`). The code’s “daylit office” interpretation is the student’s inference, not independent identification of the photograph (line 3, `model_response`). |
| Scene construction | The programs specify multiple objects: room shell, glazing, cabinets, desk, two visitor chairs, executive chair, monitor, plants and accessories. They specify colors, modeled wood-grain streaks and material settings. Chair assets group seats, backs, arms, brackets and pedestal parts; chair yaw and monitor rotations specify poses. Grouping and coordinates do not independently establish correct physical connections or appearance (lines 3 and 13, student `model_response`). |
| First correction | Step 1 failed because a chair-seat fillet radius exceeded half its smallest dimension; no image resulted (lines 4–5, `execute` and `execution_result`). The runner supplied that traceback to the student (line 6, `model_request`); the revised program reduced chair fillets and also changed the desktop plant construction and glazing emission (line 8). Step 2 advanced past the first error but failed because the scene world was `None`; again the image was null (lines 9–10). |
| Final visible execution | After receiving the second traceback (line 11), the student added world creation when absent, and also changed window placement, cabinet height, chair size and placement, foliage, and a light position. The camera parameters remained specified, with Cycles and lighting settings (lines 8 and 13). Step 3 executed; the result reports `ok: true`, a saved render and blend file, and a render log showing 16 samples despite the program specifying 48 (lines 14–15, `execute` and `execution_result`, line 15 characters [0,153439)). The runner selected step 3 (line 16, `select`). |

**Validation and outcome.** There were two observed technical execution failures followed by a successful build/render and selection—not an empty patch. Formal reconstruction correctness and visual quality remain **unknown**: no independent comparison of the image, geometry, connections, poses, camera, lighting or materials is visible. The sample-count discrepancy is observable but its cause and visual effect are unresolved. No rendered-view diagnosis or post-render student review is visible in this chunk.

**Input and exploration.** No teacher input, teacher detection, diagnosis, proposed update, or adoption is evidenced here. The trace does show runner error feedback received in subsequent requests and corresponding student revisions; these are not teacher advice. The student autonomously authored and revised programs, but the recorded sessions report zero tool calls (lines 2, 7, 12).

**Lessons and uncertainty.** Transferably, runtime feedback can distinguish invalid primitive parameters from missing scene state; successful execution alone does not validate a visual match. The particular fillet values, office layout and world initialization are task-specific. Whether the selected render matched the reference, whether its parts intersected properly, and what occurred in the unseen second chunk remain unresolved.
